title: Signature Meridian Regulator
body:
Specifications. Movement: Eight-day Signature regulator movement. Pendulum length: 0.994 metres. Overall height: 132 cm. Chime and strike: Time only. Case and dial materials: Signature walnut case, meridian dial.

Mechanism. The pendulum governs timekeeping: its swing period follows T = 2π√(L/g) with g = 9.80665 m/s², so a pendulum of 0.994 metres sets the beat rate used by the escapement. The going train carries power from the weight drum or spring barrel through geared wheels to the escapement, which meters energy to the pendulum in small, regular steps and advances the hands. Weight-driven movements need a weekly wind for an eight-day run; the weights fall slowly and evenly, and a maintaining-power device keeps the pendulum swinging while the clock is wound.

The Meridian Regulator carries a brass meridian line across its dial and a seconds subdial large enough to read from a doorway.

This is an original Signature design, created for this database and labeled signature-original. It is not presented as an authentic public or historical record.

Maintenance. Keep the clock level so the beat is even, with equal ticks on both swings. Wind on the same day each week, never forcing the key past its stop. Dust the case with a soft dry cloth, keep the movement dry and out of direct sun, and have the movement cleaned and oiled by a competent clock repairer every five to eight years. Never move a weight-driven clock with its weights hanging and its pendulum fitted.

Build and restoration guidance. Restoration starts with photographs and notes before anything is taken apart, then careful disassembly, cleaning, bushing of worn pivot holes, and reassembly in the reverse order. Replacement parts should match the original tooth counts and materials, and the finished movement is tested in beat before the dial and hands are refitted.

Tools. Clock key of the correct size, level, soft cloths, tweezers, screwdrivers sized for clock screws, oiler with clock oil, and a beat amplifier or a careful ear for beat setting.

demo.code:
import math
g = 9.80665
L = 0.994
delta = 1.0 / 1000.0

Rating change: -43.4 seconds per day

title: Signature Crown Regulator
body:
Specifications. Movement: Eight-day Signature regulator movement. Pendulum length: 0.994 metres. Overall height: 140 cm. Chime and strike: Hour strike on gong. Case and dial materials: Signature crowned mahogany case.

Mechanism. The pendulum governs timekeeping: its swing period follows T = 2π√(L/g) with g = 9.80665 m/s², so a pendulum of 0.994 metres sets the beat rate used by the escapement. The going train carries power from the weight drum or spring barrel through geared wheels to the escapement, which meters energy to the pendulum in small, regular steps and advances the hands. Weight-driven movements need a weekly wind for an eight-day run; the weights fall slowly and evenly, and a maintaining-power device keeps the pendulum swinging while the clock is wound.

Crown is the flagship Signature regulator, in crowned mahogany with a gong strike and the largest seconds subdial in the line.

This is an original Signature design, created for this database and labeled signature-original. It is not presented as an authentic public or historical record.

Maintenance. Keep the clock level so the beat is even, with equal ticks on both swings. Wind on the same day each week, never forcing the key past its stop. Dust the case with a soft dry cloth, keep the movement dry and out of direct sun, and have the movement cleaned and oiled by a competent clock repairer every five to eight years. Never move a weight-driven clock with its weights hanging and its pendulum fitted.

Build and restoration guidance. Restoration starts with photographs and notes before anything is taken apart, then careful disassembly, cleaning, bushing of worn pivot holes, and reassembly in the reverse order. Replacement parts should match the original tooth counts and materials, and the finished movement is tested in beat before the dial and hands are refitted.

Tools. Clock key of the correct size, level, soft cloths, tweezers, screwdrivers sized for clock screws, oiler with clock oil, and a beat amplifier or a careful ear for beat setting.
